page: Microsoft Azure L4aos_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Laosv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Additionally, the instance includes a substantial 2880 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not bundle any GPU hardware or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The x86_64 architecture of the AMD EPYC processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX, AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, which facilitate vector calculations and machine learning inference. Cryptographic operations are accelerated via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI instructions. The processor topology utilizes hyper-threading with 2 threads per core, backed by 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache configurations.

Performance benchmarks reveal strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core scaling is more moderate, with stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core metrics falling into the middle 50%. Memory performance presents a notable tradeoff: while large-block write bandwidth is average at 27.93 GB/sec, read-only bandwidth for both small and large blocks is weak, scoring in the bottom 25%. Similarly, database operations and static web serving throughput are relatively weak, and medium-model LLM inference is poor, though small-model text generation remains average.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the L4aos_v4 provides a dense allocation of local storage and memory relative to its 4-vCPU compute footprint, making it a resource-dense option for workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. It is best suited for memory-intensive applications, local caching layers, single-threaded text processing, and lightweight database tasks that benefit from the large 2880 GB local storage capacity and strong single-core execution.

It features 4 dedicated vCPUs (2 physical cores), 32.0 GB of RAM, and a significant 2880 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capability. The x86_64 architecture supports AVX-512 and cryptographic acceleration. Benchmarks show strong single-core CPU and text processing performance, though multi-core scaling and memory read bandwidth are weaker.
